title: Putting it together (and a look back)
idea: Combine type awareness with variables, math, and strings from earlier units — one clear habit: know your types.

exercises.prompt:
Review from earlier: what does a variable do?

name = "Mia"
options: Remembers a value so you can use it by name later
exercises.explanation: A variable stores a value under a name. Here name holds the text "Mia". (A quick look back at Unit 8.)
Numbers and - subtract: 10 - 4 = 6. Math on numbers, from Unit 10.
Joining text with + glues the pieces; the space inside "Hi " gives Hi Mia. Strings from Unit 15.

exercises.prompt:
Now the new idea together with the old. What shows?

name = "Mia"
points = 8
print(name + " has " + str(points) + " points")
exercises.explanation: name is already text; points is a number, so str(points) makes it joinable. Together: Mia has 8 points.

exercises.prompt:
What shows?

a = "12"
b = "8"
print(int(a) + int(b))
exercises.explanation: Convert both texts to numbers, then add: 12 + 8 = 20. The core skill of this unit.

exercises.prompt: Checking a value's type before using + protects you from the 'added text instead of numbers' bug.
exercises.explanation: Yes. Knowing the type tells you what + will do, so you convert when needed. That's the whole unit in one habit.

exercises.prompt: Build a program: text price "9", a quantity of 2 (a number), show 'Total: 18'.
exercises.explanation: Convert the text price with int(), multiply by the number qty into total (18), then str(total) joins into the message.

exercises.prompt: Match each tool to its one-line job.
exercises.explanation: Three conversion tools plus your old friend print(). Pick by the job you need done.

exercises.prompt: Select EVERY line that correctly shows the number result 30.
exercises.explanation: Numbers add (30), converted text adds (30), floats add (30.0, which is 30). Only the quoted line joins to 1515.

exercises.prompt: You finished Unit 16! What is the big idea to carry forward?
options: Every value is text or a number; know which, and convert with int()/float()/str() when you need to
Numbers and text are exactly the same
exercises.explanation: That's it — type awareness plus the three conversion tools. You can now avoid the joining bug and convert on purpose. Well done!
